title: pick's incumbent delta is read over unpaired runs while the pick reads paired cells
body:
## Summary
The `pick` line and report delta table compare incumbent and proposal over every current record, while the pick itself ranks over paired, outcome-conditioned cells (ADR 0145).

## Description
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/__main__.py:133 builds `stats = aggregate(interviews, scenarios)` over all current-digest records and :138 passes it to `against`; src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/pick.py `against` takes speed/accuracy/judge/usage deltas and `runs` from those stats. `_pick_cells` ranks over `paired(...)` cells and `conditioned(...)` cells. When one config completed more cells than another (the very case ADR 0145 guards), the printed delta (`first text -620 ms ... (n 18/18)`) and the reason (`fastest p50 (X ms); paired 12 of 18`) are figures over different sets. eval-harness / comparison-modes: a delta is over one declared set. Fixed: `against` takes the stats restricted to the pick's paired cells (and its conditioned speed), and `runs` says the paired n.

## Flow
- config A completes 18 cells, config B 12 (B is out on coverage or both survive on the 12 paired)
- pick reads quality over 12 paired cells, speed over the conditioned subset
- against() reads A's p50 over 18 and B's over 12 -> the delta line mixes sets

## Expected impact
The operator reading `pick` before `--write` sees a delta consistent with the reason it prints. Could break: the report's delta table numbers move for runs with uneven coverage.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the delta printed beside a pick is over the cells the pick was read over
Before: walked: delta over all records (n 18/12), reason over paired 12
After: predicted: delta and reason both over paired 12
Method: simulation - three walked cases (even coverage: identical; uneven: different n; a stale-excluded cell: different set); no run dir with uneven coverage on this machine
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/__main__.py:133 stats = aggregate(interviews, scenarios)
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/__main__.py:138 picks = against(picks, stats, shape_stats, read_tiers(tiers))
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/pick.py _pick_cells: cells = paired(known, candidates); stats = aggregate(restrict(known, candidates, cells), scenarios)
instrument: a pick test with uneven coverage (opus-low 18 cells, haiku-low 12) asserting pick.runs and delta are over the 12 paired cells

title: store.create sits outside the try in run_pair, run_interview and run_shape
body:
## Summary
A session that cannot be created raises out of the pair/job before its record exists, leaking the temp dir and leaving no dump.

## Description
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/run.py:404, src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/simulate.py:567 and :757 call `store.create(...)` after `tempfile.mkdtemp` and before the `try` whose `finally` removes the root and fills the record. A raise there (a playbook the store refuses, a disk error) escapes: `run_pairs`/`run_jobs` name the failure but write no dump, and `root` is never removed. README section 2: every job leaves its row; run.py's contract: a bench bug is that pair's failure.

## Flow
- SessionStore.create raises for one pair
- run_pair raises before try -> no dump, temp dir left
- fixed: create inside try, finally guards a None session, the dump says `failure: <Type>`

## Expected impact
A crashed pair leaves a dump that names the failure and no temp dir. Could break: nothing visible; the finally must tolerate a missing session.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed session create leaves a record and no temp dir
Before: walked: no dump, root dir leaked (three sites)
After: predicted: dump with failure, root removed
Method: simulation - read the three sites; the S instrument (a store whose create raises) was not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/run.py:404 session = store.create(pair.playbook_id, intro)  # before try
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/simulate.py:567 session = store.create(scenario.playbook_id, record["intro"])
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/simulate.py:757 session = store.create(scenario.playbook_id)
instrument: a test whose SessionStore.create raises: assert a dump/record with the failure is written and the mkdtemp root is gone

title: legs-per-interview formula is kept twice by hand and derived from neither loop
body:
## Summary
`legs_per_pair` and `Plan.legs` restate the adopt loop's leg count as arithmetic; no test derives it from the loop.

## Description
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/run.py:610 and src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/simulate.py:216 both compute `2 + (rounds - 1) * 3 + (1 if last else 3) + 1` per interview. The `--dry` leg estimates operators budget on rest on it; when athena.adopt.loop changes how many legs a card costs, both lists go stale silently (section 4.7: a hand-kept list beside the thing it lists). Fixed: one function, and a test that drives the scripted fake model through N cards and counts the legs it was asked for.

## Flow
- drive FakeModel through 1, 3 and MAX_ROUNDS cards
- count interview/audit/persona/brief prompts
- compare with the formula

## Expected impact
The dry estimate tracks the loop. Could break: the dry text's figure, if the formula is already off.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the leg estimate is derived from the loop, not restated
Before: two hand copies, zero derived tests
After: one copy, pinned by a scripted-loop count
Method: simulation - read both sites; the scripted count was not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/run.py:610 def legs_per_pair(...): onboarding = 2 + (rounds - 1) * 3 + (1 if last else 3) + 1
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/simulate.py:216 def legs(self, rounds): per = 2 + (rounds - 1) * 3 + (1 if last else 3) + 1
instrument: a test driving tests/proving/*/conftest FakeModel through 1, 3 and MAX_ROUNDS cards and counting legs against the formula

title: the tier pick ranks configs without checking the order beats run-to-run noise
body:
## Summary
`_fastest` orders configs by p50 with a 5 % tie band but never tests whether the between-config spread exceeds the within-config spread, at 2 reps.

## Description
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/pick.py:308 `_fastest` takes the minimum p50 and a fixed 5 % band. eval-harness / resolution-precondition: a ranking is published only when the between-condition spread exceeds the within-condition standard deviation; otherwise the honest output is a tie. With reps=2 over 9 scenarios, first-text p50s of neighbouring configs can sit inside each other's run-to-run spread, and `pick --write` would rewrite tiers.json on a draw. Fixed: per survivor, the within-config SD of the ranked latency; when the spread between the fastest and the next does not exceed it, the pick says `tie` and usage (or the incumbent) decides, and the report prints both figures.

## Flow
- read a run dir's interview records per config
- compute within-config SD of first_text_ms and the between-config p50 gap
- a gap under the SD is reported as a tie, not a ranking

## Expected impact
tiers.json changes only on an order the bench resolved. Could break: some current picks become ties and keep the incumbent.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a pick ranks only an order the measurement resolved
Before: no spread check; any p50 difference over 5 % ranks
After: a pick is a ranking only when the gap exceeds the within-config SD
Method: simulation - no adopt-tiers run dir on this machine to compute the two spreads; the experiment is a script over one
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/pick.py:308 def _fastest(...): best = min(...); band = [n for n in timed if speed <= best * (1 + TIE_BAND)]
TIE_BAND = 0.05; reps default 2 (src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/__main__.py:101)
instrument: a script over a proving-runs/adopt-tiers/<date>/ dir computing per-config within SD of first_text_ms and round_ms against the between-config p50 gaps

title: both benches judge Claude with a single Claude judge and no drift anchors
body:
## Summary
The chores judge (Sonnet 5.5) and the tier judge (Opus 5.5) score Claude output alone, unanchored: eval-harness / judge-stability's conflict and drift rules are unmet.

## Description
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/judge.py:47 JUDGE_TIER sonnet 5.5 judges a session whose legs, persona (src/athena/proving/chores_uat/rig.py:52) and case writer are Claude; src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/simulate.py:104 JUDGE_TIER opus 5.5 judges transcripts held by Claude configs. eval-harness golden path: 'A verdict from a single judge of the same family as the candidate is a conflict of interest'; the judge's drift is measured by re-scoring a frozen anchor set. Neither bench pins an anchor set or a second-family judge; the instrument digest pins the prompt and tier, not the judge's behaviour. Fixing it means a cross-family judge (a product decision under ADR 0007's subscription-only spend) or an anchor set re-scored per run.

## Flow
- the same judge prompt and tier score two runs a month apart
- the CLI's model silently moves
- criteria pass rates shift with no product change; nothing flags it

## Expected impact
Trend lines across fix waves stay comparable. Could break: cost (anchors re-scored each run) and a second provider's spend.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - judge verdicts comparable across time and free of same-family bias
Before: no anchors, one same-family judge
After: an anchor set re-scored per run (drift figure), or a second-family judge
Method: simulation - a direction: needs a provider/cost decision before an instrument can be built
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/judge.py:47 JUDGE_TIER = Tier(model="claude-sonnet-5-5", effort="medium")
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/simulate.py:104 JUDGE_TIER = Tier(model="claude-opus-5-5", effort="medium")
registry: software-engineering/eval-harness, technique judge-stability

title: audit usage counts the brief writer's legs while audit p50 leaves them out
body:
## Summary
The audit row's usage includes brief-writer legs (ledger trigger adopt.audit), but its audit p50 filters them out (TapRunner role 'brief').

## Description
src/athena/adopt/legs.py `_account` records trigger `adopt.<kind>`, and the brief writer is an audit-kind leg, so src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/score.py:306 `usage_of(record, ['audit'])` sums it; src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/simulate.py TapRunner marks the same leg role 'brief', and score.py:338 `audit_ms` keeps role == 'audit' only. One table row then reads cost over audit+brief and latency over audit alone. Fixed: one rule for both (either both include the brief writer, as dry_text says the role does, or both exclude it), named in the table header.

## Flow
- one interview: 3 audit legs + 1 brief leg
- usage audit = 4 legs' cost
- audit p50 = 3 legs' ms

## Expected impact
The audit row's cost and latency describe the same legs. Could break: the usage figure or p50 shown for audit moves.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one row's figures cover the same legs
Before: usage over 4 legs, latency over 3 (walked)
After: both over the same set
Method: simulation - walked one record shape; the S test is two asserts on score_interview
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/score.py:338 audit_ms = [... if leg.get("role") == "audit" ...]
src/athena/proving/adopt_tiers/simulate.py:365 "role": "brief" if system == BRIEF_SYSTEM else kind
src/athena/adopt/legs.py _account: trigger=f"adopt.{result.kind}"
instrument: a score_interview test with audit and brief legs and their ledger rows asserting usage legs == latency legs for the audit role

title: the numbers audit's desktop mirror is pinned by hand, with no test derived from the TS
body:
## Summary
numbers.py restates worth.ts / model.ts / topic.tsx arithmetic; its tests pin hand-computed rows, so a desktop change goes unnoticed (as ADR 0213's did until this round).

## Description
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/numbers.py mirrors `annualValue`, `verdictOf`, `worthOf`, `fitRows`, `usd`, `minutes`, `speedup`; tests/proving/chores_uat/test_numbers.py pins three playbooks 'by hand' from the TS. This round found the mirror one ADR behind (fixed for the ranking). The ground truth is the desktop's own functions: a vitest that renders every shipped playbook's page lines to a JSON fixture, and a pytest that compares numbers.headline(row) to it, would derive the test from the product. Out of this round's write set (apps/desktop).

## Flow
- vitest: for each shipped playbook, write worthOf/verdictOf/valueCell/fitRows output to a fixture
- pytest: headline(number_row(...)) == fixture lines, every playbook
- a desktop change that moves a figure turns the pytest red

## Expected impact
The chores judge always reads the page that ships. Could break: a fixture the desktop suite must regenerate on intended changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the mirror's test is derived from the desktop's functions
Before: 3 of 100 pages pinned by hand; drift found one ADR late
After: 100 of 100 compared against the desktop's own output
Method: simulation - the instrument spans apps/desktop and tests/proving, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tests/proving/chores_uat/test_numbers.py:1 "three real playbooks pinned by hand"
this round: 30b18004 (numbers.py was pre-ADR 0213: quarter, rank.annualUsd, Not ranked)
instrument: a vitest emitting every shipped playbook's page lines from worth.ts/model.ts to a JSON fixture, and a pytest comparing numbers.headline over the library to it

title: the judge's voice check refuses outside 60-260 words but says 80-200
body:
## Summary
check_judge tells the judge 'voice must be 80-200 words' while it accepts 60-260, so the stated rule and the enforced one differ.

## Description
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/judge.py:62 VOICE_WORDS = (60, 260); :76 the system prompt asks 80-200; :265 the retry note says 'voice must be 80-200 words; it has {words}' and fires only under 60 or over 260. A 70-word voice passes; a 59-word one is told it needs 80. The tolerance is undocumented. Fixed: name the tolerance once (a comment and the note: 'asked 80-200, refused outside 60-260'), or enforce what is asked.

## Flow
- judge answers with a 70-word voice
- check passes (60 <= 70)
- the prompt said 80-200

## Expected impact
The retry note states the bound it enforces. Could break: tightening to 80-200 would send more judge answers back (cost).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stated bound is the enforced bound
Before: asked 80-200, enforced 60-260, message 80-200
After: message names both, or one bound
Method: simulation - read the three lines; the choice between tolerance and enforcement is the operator's
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/judge.py:62 VOICE_WORDS = (60, 260)
src/athena/proving/chores_uat/judge.py:265 return f"voice must be 80-200 words; it has {words}"
